raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, a few Triton/Gluon kernels still JIT-compile inside the first user requests after startup, adding 0.5–2.6 s to those requests:

1. `VLLM_ROCM_GEMM_JIT_WARMUP`: warms up the Triton GEMM variants used by the ROCm unquantized GEMM path and the bf16x3 router GEMM for the configured batch sizes (MiniMax-M3: `_reduce_terms_kernel`, 864 warm-up calls over 16 shapes, 2.65 s at startup instead of during serving).
2. MiniMax-M3 on ROCm: warms up the sparse paged-attention decode variants (`ONE_SHOT` × context-lengths pointer alignment) that otherwise compile while serving. Alignment variants arise only where KV heads per rank are not a multiple of 4 (TP2/4/8). 4 calls, ~0.9 s per rank at startup.

Default behaviour is unchanged unless the env / model path enables it. Main has a JIT warm-up registry (`kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup`) and a Blackwell-only `_warmup_bf16x3_router_gemm`; happy to hang (1) off that registry and extend the router warm-up to ROCm if preferred.

## Test Result

MiniMax-M3 VL on MI355X, TP4: with both, no GEMM or sparse-PA compile while serving in any of 8 full benchmark passes (before: a compile inside a measured row in every pass, costing that row up to ~14%). Throughput effect is within pass-to-pass noise; the claim is the removed in-request compile, shown by the server logs. MMMU 0.636–0.678.
Known gap: the LM head's AITER `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` variants still compile on first use; not covered here.
raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [ROCm] Warm up Triton GEMM and MiniMax-M3 sparse-PA decode variants that otherwise compile inside the first requests

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Connect loaded MiniMax-M3 ROCm sparse attention layers to the warmup of
+their AITER sparse paged-attention decode kernel."""
+
+import sys
+import time
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker import Worker
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def minimax_m3_rocm_sparse_pa_warmup(worker: "Worker") -> None:
+    model_module = sys.modules.get("vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model")
+    if model_module is None:
+        return
+
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.sparse_pa import (
+        minimax_m3_sparse_attn_aiter_warmup,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.sparse_attention_msa import (
+        MiniMaxM3SparseAiterPAImpl,
+    )
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    seen: set[tuple] = set()
+    row_counts: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+    for layer in worker.get_model().modules():
+        if not isinstance(layer, model_module.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention):
+            continue
+        impl = layer.impl
+        # Without the table buffers the indexer emits into, the attend gets
+        # freshly allocated (aligned) tables; that path is not warmed here.
+        if (
+            not layer.use_aiter_sparse_pa
+            or not isinstance(impl, MiniMaxM3SparseAiterPAImpl)
+            or layer.sparse_bt_buffer is None
+            or layer.sparse_ctx_buffer is None
+            or layer.kv_cache.numel() == 0
+        ):
+            continue
+        k_cache, v_cache = layer.get_aiter_sparse_pa_kv_cache()
+        k_scale = getattr(layer, "_k_scale", None) if impl.use_fp8_kv else None
+        v_scale = getattr(layer, "_v_scale", None) if impl.use_fp8_kv else None
+        # One allocation of the table buffers serves every layer, so the layers
+        # differ at most in their cache views.
+        key = (
+            impl.num_heads,
+            impl.num_kv_heads,
+            k_cache.dtype,
+            tuple(k_cache.shape),
+            tuple(v_cache.shape),
+            None if k_scale is None else tuple(k_scale.shape),
+            layer.sparse_bt_buffer.data_ptr(),
+            layer.sparse_ctx_buffer.data_ptr(),
+        )
+        if key in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(key)
+        row_counts = minimax_m3_sparse_attn_aiter_warmup(
+            k_cache,
+            v_cache,
+            layer.sparse_bt_buffer,
+            layer.sparse_ctx_buffer,
+            impl.num_heads,
+            impl.num_kv_heads,
+            impl.head_size,
+            impl.scale,
+            worker.model_config.dtype,
+            k_scale,
+            v_scale,
+        )
+    if not seen:
+        return
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    logger.info(
+        "Warmed up MiniMax-M3 AITER sparse PA decode for %d cache layout(s) at "
+        "%s rows, context lengths aligned and not, in %.2fs.",
+        len(seen),
+        row_counts,
+        time.perf_counter() - start,
+    )

@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Compile before serving the Triton variants that ROCm's unquantized GEMM dispatch
+and the bf16x3 MoE router would otherwise JIT-compile inside the first requests.
+
+Triton specializes integer arguments on ``== 1`` and on divisibility by 16, and the
+startup forwards (profile run, CUDA-graph capture) use token counts that are mostly
+multiples of 16. The first real prefill or mixed step with another count then compiles
+another variant in the middle of the step. On MiniMax-M3 (gfx950) these are the bf16x3
+router reduction at >= 2048 tokens and AITER's tuned Triton GEMM of the dense MLP, each
+about a second, which shows up as a TTFT spike on the first requests after a server
+start. This calls the same dispatchers the layers use, at token counts on both sides
+of every specialization boundary, so whatever Triton kernel they pick is compiled here.
+"""
+
+import time
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker import Worker
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# 1-32 tokens (skinny kernels, tuned rows padded to 16 / 32) and both sides of the
+# powers of two up to 4096 (the bf16x3 router starts at 2048 tokens).
+_TOKEN_COUNTS = (
+    tuple(range(1, 33))
+    + tuple(m for p in (64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) for m in (p - 1, p, p + 1))
+    + (2064,)
+)
+
+
+def _enabled() -> bool:
+    import vllm.envs as envs
+
+    return envs.VLLM_ROCM_GEMM_JIT_WARMUP
+
+
+def rocm_gemm_jit_warmup(worker: "Worker") -> None:
+    if not (current_platform.is_rocm() and _enabled()):
+        return
+
+    import vllm.envs as envs
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.gate_linear import GateLinear
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import LinearBase, UnquantizedLinearMethod
+
+    if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:
+        return
+
+    max_tokens = worker.scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens
+    counts = sorted(m for m in _TOKEN_COUNTS if m <= max_tokens)
+    seen: set[tuple] = set()
+    calls = 0
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        for module in worker.get_model().modules():
+            if isinstance(module, GateLinear):
+                weight_split = getattr(module, "_bf16x3_weight", None)
+                if not getattr(module, "allow_rocm_bf16x3_router_gemm", False) or (
+                    weight_split is None
+                ):
+                    continue
+                weight = module.weight
+                key = ("router", tuple(weight.shape), weight.dtype)
+                if key in seen:
+                    continue
+                seen.add(key)
+                for m in counts:
+                    x = torch.zeros(
+                        m, weight.shape[1], dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=weight.device
+                    )
+                    torch.ops.vllm.rocm_bf16x3_router_gemm_dispatch(
+                        x, weight, weight_split
+                    )
+                    calls += 1
+                continue
+            if not isinstance(module, LinearBase) or not isinstance(
+                getattr(module, "quant_method", None), UnquantizedLinearMethod
+            ):
+                continue
+            weight = getattr(module, "weight", None)
+            if (
+                not isinstance(weight, torch.Tensor)
+                or weight.dim() != 2
+                or weight.dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16)
+                or not weight.is_cuda
+            ):
+                continue
+            bias = getattr(module, "bias", None)
+            # Row-parallel layers add the bias on rank 0 only: warm both variants.
+            for b in (None, bias) if isinstance(bias, torch.Tensor) else (None,):
+                key = (
+                    "linear",
+                    tuple(weight.shape),
+                    tuple(weight.stride()),
+                    weight.dtype,
+                    b is not None,
+                )
+                if key in seen:
+                    continue
+                seen.add(key)
+                for m in counts:
+                    x = torch.zeros(
+                        m, weight.shape[1], dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device
+                    )
+                    torch.ops.vllm.rocm_unquantized_gemm(x, weight, b)
+                    calls += 1
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    logger.info(
+        "ROCm GEMM JIT warmup: %d calls over %d weight shapes, token counts %d-%d, "
+        "in %.2fs.",
+        calls,
+        len(seen),
+        counts[0],
+        counts[-1],
+        time.perf_counter() - start,
+    )

@@ -630,3 +630,73 @@ def _run_gluon_decode(
         sliding_window=-1,
         ps=True,
     )
+
+
+# Rows of the warmup's small call: several context partitions per row, and no
+# specialization on == 1.
+_WARMUP_FEW_ROWS = 3
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def minimax_m3_sparse_attn_aiter_warmup(
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    v_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    sparse_bt_buffer: torch.Tensor,  # [max_tokens * num_kv_heads, width] int32
+    sparse_ctx_buffer: torch.Tensor,  # [max_tokens * num_kv_heads] int32
+    num_heads: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    head_size: int,
+    sm_scale: float,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    v_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Compile the variants of AITER's Gluon decode kernel that serving reaches
+    but the startup forwards do not, and return the row counts it called.
+
+    Two properties of a call select the variant:
+    - ``ONE_SHOT`` (one context partition per row) holds once a call has at
+      least as many rows (tokens x KV heads) as the GPU runs programs at once.
+      Decode batches usually stay below that, and a prefill short enough for
+      the dense MSA path never reaches the sparse attend.
+    - The alignment of the context lengths. A prefill's rows follow the decode
+      rows in the table buffers the indexer fills, so when the decode token
+      count times KV heads is not a multiple of 4 the pointer is not 16-byte
+      aligned, and Triton specializes on that.
+    Each variant takes seconds to compile, a TTFT spike on the request that
+    meets it. This calls the attend on the layer's own cache and table buffers
+    (their contents are rewritten before every use) at both row counts and
+    both alignments.
+    """
+    from aiter.ops.triton.gluon.pa_decode_gluon import get_recommended_splits
+
+    kvh = num_kv_heads
+    max_rows = sparse_ctx_buffer.shape[0] // kvh - 1
+    many = _WARMUP_FEW_ROWS
+    while get_recommended_splits(many * kvh, 1) > 1 and many < max_rows:
+        many *= 2
+    row_counts = tuple(n for n in (_WARMUP_FEW_ROWS, many) if n <= max_rows)
+    for n in row_counts:
+        q = torch.zeros(
+            n, num_heads, head_size, dtype=dtype, device=sparse_ctx_buffer.device
+        )
+        out = torch.empty_like(q)
+        # From row 0 (aligned) and from row 1, as after an odd decode count.
+        for first in (0, 1):
+            sparse_bt = sparse_bt_buffer[first * kvh : (first + n) * kvh]
+            sparse_ctx = sparse_ctx_buffer[first * kvh : (first + n) * kvh]
+            sparse_bt.zero_()  # page 0 exists in every cache view
+            sparse_ctx.fill_(ASM_PAGE_SIZE)  # one page
+            _run_gluon_decode(
+                q,
+                k_cache,
+                v_cache,
+                sparse_bt,
+                sparse_ctx,
+                kvh,
+                sm_scale,
+                out,
+                k_scale,
+                v_scale,
+            )
+    return row_counts
